### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **2** package(s): `@objectstack/metadata-protocol`, `@objectstack/spec`, touching **26** documentable anchor(s).

**31** hand-written doc(s) name something this change touched — list omitted above 15 rows. Re-derive on the tree named below: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 702c562c1f82b3e5fec9bd4c2bc978604740e033`.

⛔ **11** release-owned page(s) also affected — read-only, see AGENTS.md Documentation Guardrails.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **1** anchor(s) matched too much of the corpus to be a work list: `/meta/:type/:name (route, 47 pages)`
- **7** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **65** of **247** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **182** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **182**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **59** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **123** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **172** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 702c562c1f82b3e5fec9bd4c2bc978604740e033` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `7bbdcc3130967317980922a2f466cf6a8e2e89f1` — the merge of head `8715fcedd22ac73dceb41e546fbacbb1c822f47f` into base `702c562c1f82b3e5fec9bd4c2bc978604740e033`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 7bbdcc3130967317980922a2f466cf6a8e2e89f1 && git checkout 7bbdcc3130967317980922a2f466cf6a8e2e89f1
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 702c562c1f82b3e5fec9bd4c2bc978604740e033 8715fcedd22ac73dceb41e546fbacbb1c822f47f && git checkout -B drift-repro 702c562c1f82b3e5fec9bd4c2bc978604740e033 && git merge --no-ff 8715fcedd22ac73dceb41e546fbacbb1c822f47f

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 702c562c1f82b3e5fec9bd4c2bc978604740e033
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs 702c562c1f82b3e5fec9bd4c2bc978604740e033` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `1484f1cd42f1e8e9f763c99d9fc5cbb4ce197f14`
Local-runs: none
Scope: .changeset/32820-reenable-heals-holder-slot.md, .changeset/32820-reenable-heal-upgrade-guide-entry.md, packages/metadata-protocol/src/protocol-registry-hydration.ts, packages/metadata-protocol/src/protocol.lookup-artifact-item-call-sites.test.ts, packages/metadata-protocol/src/protocol.register-item-call-sites.test.ts, packages/objectql/src/package-scoped-exact-qualifier.test.ts, packages/spec/src/migrations/entries/semantic/18.package-less-overlay-row-holder-slot-on-reenable.ts + read as cited code, not reviewed: `hydrateOverlayIntoRegistry` and `soleHolderOf` outside the diff and the hydrator's three callers, `declinesStoredRow` and `isUnservedSealedOverlay` in packages/metadata-protocol/src/protocol-lock-state.ts, `isSealedManagedItem` in packages/metadata-protocol/src/protocol-write-gates.ts, `PACKAGE_SCOPED_TYPES` in packages/core/src/package-scoped-resolution.ts, `getItem`, `enablePackage` and `onPackageEnabled` in packages/objectql/src/registry.ts, the `replacement` of packages/spec/src/migrations/entries/semantic/18.package-less-row-exact-address-by-type-class.ts.

First-round review, read at 2026-11-13T20:27Z. Inputs: card #32820, the PR title and body as they stand, the diff against the merge base `bf02d33b` (seven files, +277 −6), the check-runs on this head, the knock 6863438812. Claim 6863460858.

### ① Derived judgments

- The title, the body and the first changeset agree: `fix(metadata-protocol)!:`, `Clause-②: no (narrowing)`, `Metadata-protocol: narrowed`, the BREAKING banner, `adr-0087: registered`, and a `Skills-docs: none` line with its reason. `no` is right: the heal is module-internal and the diff adds no export.
- The second changeset carries the ledger entry alone and reads `Clause-②: no`, `Metadata-protocol: none`. Right.
- The declared move is the one the code makes for the three overlay types: after the enable, a holder's registry item, the list scoped to it and the registry list answer its own item. Nothing that was refused is served; the exact read is not touched.
- The record is not limited to those three types (s1). No fourth type can move today.

### ② Semver level

- `minor` on `@objectstack/metadata-protocol`, `patch` on `@objectstack/spec`: right for a `narrowed` kind. `@objectstack/objectql` carries test changes only and takes no bump.
- `Check Changeset` is green on this body.

### ③ Boundary flags

- Check-runs on this head, all concluded: 67 runs, 56 success, 11 skipped, none failed. The eight `Test Core` shards and their roll-up, the type checks and `Check Changeset` are green.
- Order. The merge base is `bf02d33b`; `main` is five commits past it (#33142, #33143, #33144, #33121, #33129), none on a path of this diff. A `git merge-tree` of `main` and this head reports no conflict.
- The body carries one residue with no card: a holder installed, not re-enabled, after the hydration keeps the row in the other holder's slot until the next unscoped hydration. It needs `packages/objectql/src/registry.ts`, outside this card's surface. The seat's to file or leave.
- The mirror case is `main`'s and not this card's: a disable sends no notice, so a row hydrated with both holders served stays without an envelope until the next hydration.
- The ablations, the local runs and the dogfood battery are the report's; none was run here.

### ④ Design judgment

`packages/metadata-protocol/src/protocol-registry-hydration.ts`. The hydrator records what it built an entry from at the one place it registers, and only for a package-less row that wears a sole holder's envelope; any other registration of the key through the hydrator forgets the record. The heal then calls the hydrator's own three steps (`soleHolderOf`, the artifact lookup, `mergeArtifactProtection` over `stateTenantAuthorship(withRowBinding(data, undefined))`), so the rebuilt entry is the one a hydration would build for the holders served at the enable. That is the right way to keep one builder. The identity guard reads the bare slot at the row's own bundle member and compares the object, so a later write, delete or hydration owns the slot and the heal steps aside. The subscription is taken once per registry, on the first record, and uses the registry's existing enable notice, which fires only for a package that was disabled; the heal is synchronous, and the hydrator has no `await` between its holder count and its registration, so the two cannot interleave.

`packages/spec/src/migrations/entries/semantic/18.package-less-overlay-row-holder-slot-on-reenable.ts`. The printed fields carry no tracker id. The remedy order (keep the body, clear a bound row, delete the package-less row, then save the declared override in the pair) is the order `package-less-row-exact-address-by-type-class` prescribes, and the entry says why the delete goes first.

`packages/objectql/src/package-scoped-exact-qualifier.test.ts`. Three types in both registration orders, each asserting the disabled period first (A's slot reads the row) and then all three readers at both holders, the slot's stamp, and the unchanged 409. The three CONTROLs can fail, and the report's two ablations hold the heal and the guard apart. Two of the heal's outcomes run in no pin (s2).

Findings:

- **s1 should-fix. The record has no type list; the declaration has three types.** By reading, a package-less `permission` row is the fourth: `isUnservedSealedOverlay` excepts `permission`, so the row is not declined, it wears its sole holder's envelope, and the record takes it. Two holders of a permission set are refused by the registry today (the suite reaches that state only through `admitSecondPermissionHolder`), so nothing moves now. When that rule opens, the heal moves a type the changeset and the ledger entry do not name. Owed: either a sentence in the changeset saying so, or a pin of `permission` behind that switch, or the record limited to the declared types.
- **s2 should-fix.** The heal has four outcomes: the slot is no longer the recorded object, the holder is unchanged, two holders are served, and one other holder (or none) is served. The pins run the first three. The fourth rebuilds the entry under another holder's envelope and records it again: A and B hold, B disabled, the hydrator runs, A disabled, B enabled. One pin of that sequence, with A enabled after it, would run the re-record and the second heal.
- **n1 nit.** When no holder is served at the enable, the heal rebuilds through the lookup that names no package and drops the record, whatever envelope the rebuilt entry wears. If that lookup answers a disabled holder's artifact, the next enable has nothing to rebuild. As the hydrator would leave it; the seat may route it with the install residue or leave it.

No must-fix.

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`

Local-runs: none
Scope: packages/metadata-protocol/src/protocol-registry-hydration.ts, packages/objectql/src/package-scoped-exact-qualifier.test.ts (the interdiff), and the PR body's declaration lines + read as cited code, not reviewed: `hydrateOverlayIntoRegistry` and `healSoleHolderEnvelopes` outside the interdiff, `PACKAGE_SCOPED_TYPES` in packages/core/src/package-scoped-resolution.ts; otherwise nothing beyond what record 6864058135 lists

Delta review of PASS 6864058135, read at 2026-11-13T21:44Z. Inputs: the interdiff `1484f1cd..8715fced` (one commit of this branch on two files, no merge), the PR title and body as they stand after the body edit of 21:41Z, the check-runs on this head, knock 6865628488. Claim 6865104036. Everything that record judged and the interdiff does not touch stands as read there.

### ① Derived judgments

- The declaration stands: `Clause-②: no (narrowing)`, `Metadata-protocol: narrowed`, `Skills-docs: none`, the BREAKING banner, the `!` title, `adr-0087: registered`. The interdiff moves no answer a deployment can reach today: it takes `permission` out of the heal's reach, and the registry refuses a second holder of a permission set, so no `permission` record could ever meet a second served holder.
- After the interdiff the code and the changeset name the same three types (`email_template`, `dashboard`, `report`).

### ② Semver level

- Unchanged and right: `minor` on `@objectstack/metadata-protocol`, `patch` on `@objectstack/spec`.

### ③ Boundary flags

- Check-runs on this head, all concluded: 71 runs, 58 success, 13 skipped, none failed. The 67 runs of the push: 56 success, 11 skipped; the eight `Test Core` shards and their roll-up, the type checks and `Check Changeset` are green. The four newest are the re-runs the body edit started at 21:41Z: `Check Changeset` success, the PR-body guards success, `Auto Label` and `Check PR Size` skipped.
- Order. The merge base is still `bf02d33b`; `main` is at `b22be279`, eight commits past it (#33142, #33143, #33144, #33121, #33129, #33145, #33146 and the `validate_expression` fix at its tip), none on a path of this diff. A `git merge-tree` of `main` and this head reports no conflict.
- The body is restated for this head: eleven pins in the `[#32820]` group, the round 2 ablations (type limit, heal, re-record), 61 of 61 gates over the two changed files, the dogfood battery. Those runs are the report's; none was run here. One ablation leg reports its build exiting 1 at the declaration step with the marker proved in the built files; the restore build exited 0.
- The install residue (a holder installed, not re-enabled, after the hydration) still has no card, as flagged in record 6864058135. The seat's.

### ④ Design judgment

`packages/metadata-protocol/src/protocol-registry-hydration.ts` (s1). Closed. `HEALED_OVERLAY_TYPES` limits the record to the three declared types, read against the canonical type at the one place a record is written. By reading, the types that reached the record before were those three and `permission` (the package-scoped types whose stored row the hydrator does not decline and whose artifact envelope it grafts), so the list removes `permission` and nothing else. The new pin opens the second permission holder through the test switch and asserts the enable leaves the hydrated entry as the same object; without the list the heal would build it again, so the pin can fail.

`packages/objectql/src/package-scoped-exact-qualifier.test.ts` (s2). Closed. The new pin walks the holder set from A alone to B alone to both, and reads the entry under A's envelope, then under B's, then each holder's own item on all three readers. That is the `holder` string arm of `healSoleHolderEnvelopes` (the record kept under the new holder) followed by the two-holder arm, which no pin ran before.

Findings:

- **n1 nit, carried from record 6864058135.** The no-holder outcome of the heal still drops the record. The body now names it under Carried, beside the install residue. No change asked.
- **n2 nit, new.** `HEALED_OVERLAY_TYPES` is a hand-written list beside the condition that decides which rows wear a sole holder's envelope. A type that later joins that set (package-scoped, its stored row not declined) would wear the envelope and get no heal, and no test would fail; the list's comment names only `permission`. A pin that reads the two sets side by side would close it. No change asked on this PR.

One reading left with the seat, no change asked: the `permission` pin states today's behaviour under the test switch (the hydrated entry stays in the first holder's slot after the enable). That is the residue this card closes for the other three types. The change that opens a second holder of a permission set owes the widening, and this pin and the list's comment are where it will meet it.

s1 and s2 of record 6864058135 are closed on this head. No must-fix, no should-fix.
